Subject: Acme POC - Integration & Success Criteria (post-call recap)

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same plan for the POC/trial: 

High-level goal:
- Validate Redwood Inference for Acme's customer-facing summarization and retrieval workflow (end-to-end). Focus is on latency, cost per token, and fidelity to your accuracy requirements.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
- Latency: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 700ms for 1k token generation (under expected load).
- Throughput: support burst to 50 rps and sustained 10-20 rps.
- Quality: Rouge-L/ROUGE-like reference checks + manual QA for 200 sample prompts; no more than 10% unacceptable outputs defined by your QA rubric.
- Cost target: unit token cost below your internal threshold (to be confirmed).
- Security: data-in-transit encrypted; model execution in a dedicated VPC (if needed) or hosted with SOC2 controls.

POC scope & deliverables:
- Week 0: kickoff, access + credentials, share integration checklist.
- Week 1-2: integration (SDK + streaming test, initial prompts + eval harness).
- Week 3: load/latency tests and quality evaluation; iterate on prompts/config (batching, quantization recommendations).
- Week 4: POC wrap + runbook and next steps (Dedicated or Private options).

Owners & next actions:
- Redwood AE: Marissa (owner for timelines, commercial).
- Redwood SE: Dev (technical onboarding, SDK snippets, integration checklist).
- Acme: Aisha (POC owner), Tom (engineering lead).

Immediate asks from our side:
1) Confirm the success criteria above (latency / throughput / quality / cost).
2) Confirm who on your side will run the evaluation (name/email).
3) Preferred kickoff window next week (we suggested Tue/Wed).

I'm attaching the integration checklist and a draft MPA for your procurement team to review. I can schedule the kickoff once you confirm timing.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Confirmed evaluation metrics (will use these for scoring):
- Latency: p50 < 250ms, p95 < 600ms (we can relax p50 slightly if cost improvements are significant).
- Throughput: sustain 30 rps during peak tests; support 60 rps for short bursts (30s).
- Accuracy: We will run 250 samples from our internal gold set; pass threshold is 90% by our QA rubric (binary acceptable/unacceptable).
- Cost: please provide an estimate for both hosted (per-token) and dedicated (monthly) scenarios so we can compare.

Technical & security items:
- We would prefer the initial integration via Redwood hosted API with TLS and org-level access tokens. If performance requires it, we'll evaluate Dedicated (VPC) option.
- Data retention: can you confirm logs retention defaults and options for deletion upon request?
- Does the SDK support streaming responses and function/tool calling for structured extraction? We will need streaming for our live summarization UI and function calling for downstream slot-filling.

Timeline & kickoff:
- Aisha (me) is the POC owner. Tom will lead engineering. We can kickoff Tue Mar 17 or Wed Mar 18 (ET morning works best).

Please have your SE provide an integration checklist and sample SDK routes (Node/cURL) for streaming and function calling. Also, share the sample eval harness or repo if possible.

Thanks — looking forward to starting.

Best,
Aisha Khan

Subject: Redwood SDK + Streaming & Function-Calling: quick integration notes

Hi Aisha / Tom —

Quick technical notes to help your engineers get started. Happy to jump on a short 30-min tech kickoff during the week of Mar 17 as well.

1) Auth & endpoints
- Hosted API: POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate (Bearer token)
- Dedicated: will provide a private endpoint per deployment (usually https://<customer>.redwood-internal/v1/generate)

2) SDKs
- NodeJS (npm package @redwood/inference) supports streaming and function calling. Example (streaming):

const client = require('@redwood/inference');
const c = client({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
const stream = c.generateStream({ model: 'redwood-1-large', prompt: 'Summarize...', max_tokens: 500 });
stream.on('data', chunk => console.log(chunk.text));
stream.on('end', () => console.log('done'));

- cURL streaming example:

curl -N \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \n  -d '{"model":"redwood-1-large","prompt":"Summarize...","stream":true}'

3) Function/tool calling (structured extraction)
- We expose a function-calling parameter where you declare expected output schema and Redwood returns a machine-parsable JSON payload. Example payload: {"name":"extract_slots","arguments":{"customer_name":"...","summary":"..."}}
- SDKs include helpers to validate and map outputs back to your services. If you use streaming + function-calls, we buffer until the function payload is complete and then emit the final structured call.

4) Recommended routes & batching settings (initial)
- For your POC: single-token streaming, batch_size: auto (start with 8), max_concurrent_requests: 25. These settings target low tail latency while keeping GPU utilization efficient.

5) Profiling & telemetry
- If you share a 100-sample prompt set and a traffic shape (rps timeline), we can run a profiling job on our hosted baseline and share p50/p95 numbers and cost estimate.

6) Data handling & retention
- By default logs retained 30 days; request-driven deletion supported. Payloads are encrypted at rest; we can sign an addendum for additional controls if you need Private/VPC.

7) Attachments & sample repos
- Integration checklist (sent by Marissa).
- Sample eval harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/poc-eval-harness

If helpful, I can include a minimal Node example repo with streaming + function-calling wired to a simple UI.

Cheers,
